        2 Open Pathway<span class="aoi-s">s</span></a></nav> <main class="submit-aol" data-v-7e02d120><header class="blue"><div class="row max-6"><div class="text"><div class="richtext lead"><h6>Responses Due By</h6> <p>2026-08-10 23:59:59 US/Eastern Time</p> <!----></div> <div class="heading"><h6 class="eyebrow">Work With Us - Commercial Companies - Submit Solution</h6> <h1>Suitable Warfighting Adaptive Payloads (SWAP-USV)</h1> <p></p><hr style="border:none; border-top:solid 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.25); margin-top: 70px; margin-bottom: 30px;"><p></p> <p>We look forward to your solution —<br>To submit, scroll to the form at the bottom of this page.</p></div></div></div></header> <section class="info"><div class="row" style="display:block;"><div class="description"><h3>Project Description</h3> <div class="interest"><h3><strong style="font-family: Lato, sans-serif; font-size: 13pt; color: rgb(31, 31, 31); background-color: transparent;">Problem</strong></h3><p><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(31, 31, 31); background-color: transparent;">The cost-exchange ratio for detecting and neutralizing asymmetric maritime threats in contested environments is heavily skewed in favor of the adversary. Bad actors deploy low-cost, low-signature threats—including explosive Unmanned Surface Vessels (USVs), Group 1–3 Unmanned Aircraft System (UASs), "go-fast" smuggling boats, and semi-submersibles.</span></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(31, 31, 31); background-color: transparent;">Currently, the Department of War (DoW) relies on exquisite, multi-million-dollar naval and aviation assets to intercept these inexpensive targets. The Government requires affordable, scalable, production-ready maritime systems capable of persistent search, tracking, and operational effects against asymmetric threats. The Government seeks innovation combinations of USVs and UASs that maximize operational effectiveness while improving the cost-exchange ratio across a range of mission profiles. </span></p><p><br></p><h3><strong style="font-family: Lato, sans-serif; font-size: 13pt; color: rgb(31, 31, 31); background-color: transparent;">Solution</strong></h3><p><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(31, 31, 31); background-color: transparent;">The Government and the Department of War Innovation Unit (DIU) seek to partner with established maritime manufacturers, autonomy developers, sensor manufacturers, and UAS developers to execute a multi-phase Prize Challenge under 10 USC 4025 with up to $100M in available funding.</span></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(31, 31, 31); background-color: transparent;">The DoW is relying on industry to provide inexpensive and scalable solutions that combine proven USVs with mature drone capabilities to extend sensing, targeting, communications, and defeat of hostile threats through kinetic and non-kinetic effects at scale. </span></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(31, 31, 31); background-color: transparent;">This competition will be executed as a </span><strong style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(31, 31, 31); background-color: transparent;">12-Month Prize Challenge with rolling submission windows</strong><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(31, 31, 31); background-color: transparent;"> divided into three Sprint cohorts. In order to be considered for Sprint 1, submissions must be received by 8/10/2026 @ 2359 EST. Future submission windows will be published after the completion of Sprint 1. See “Challenge Series & Rolling Sprints” for additional details.</span></p><p><br></p><p><strong style="font-family: Lato, sans-serif; font-size: 13pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;">Desired Solution Attributes</strong></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(31, 31, 31); background-color: transparent;">The Department of War (DoW) seeks mature, market-ready USVs fully integrated with two or more mature, market-ready aerial drones to detect, identify, track, and defeat hostile threats. This program aims to fill a critical gap in low cost sensing and defeat within the maritime environment. </span></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;">The USV solution must demonstrate a minimum operational range of 200 nautical miles and a sustained cruise speed of at least 10 knots. These </span><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(34, 34, 34); background-color: transparent;">values represent threshold requirements for consideration; however, the government seeks the highest-performing solutions, and top performers are expected to substantially exceed these minimums. </span></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(34, 34, 34); background-color: transparent;">The USV solution </span><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;">should enable the following operations:</span></p><p><br></p><ol><li><span style="font-size: 11pt; background-color: transparent;">Carry, launch, control, and employ a minimum of two UAS, collectively capable of kinetic strike with a minimum 2kg payload and battle damage assessment (BDA). The UAS should include multiple system types to include a mix of recoverable/reusable and single use/one-way attack (OWA). The UASs should be technically mature and have an established production line. </span></li><li><span style="font-size: 11pt; background-color: transparent;">Navigation to user-defined waypoints, patrol designated areas, loiter on station, and reposition in response to operator commands or mission objectives. </span></li><li><span style="font-size: 11pt; background-color: transparent;">Safely operate in blue water, littoral, and brown water environments.</span></li><li><span style="font-size: 11pt; background-color: transparent;">Detect, identify, and track surface targets using onboard sensors and/or launched drones, providing operators with real time situational awareness and the ability to direct drone employment as required.</span></li></ol><p><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;">The UAS solution should enable the following operations:</span></p><p><br></p><ol><li><span style="color: rgb(31, 31, 31); font-size: 11pt; background-color: transparent;">Seamless launch from the USV</span><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-size: 11pt; background-color: transparent;">.</span></li><li><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(31, 31, 31); background-color: transparent;">If utilizing expendable or loitering munitions, the design emphasizes a low cost per operational effect and fail-safe mission-abort protocols to prevent unexploded ordnance hazards.</span></li><li><span style="font-size: 11pt; background-color: transparent;">Detect, classify, and maintain persistent custody of threats at extended ranges. Drones should support one or more operational effects, including ISR, comms relay, electronic warfare, payload delivery, or precision engagement of moving or stationary, as applicable, under operator command.   </span></li><li><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(31, 31, 31); background-color: transparent;">If recoverable, the UAS should be capable of safe and repeatable recovery aboard the USV while underway and in representative sea states with minimal operator intervention</span></li></ol><p><strong style="font-family: Lato, sans-serif; font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;">Desired Primary Attributes</strong></p><p><br></p><p class="ql-indent-1"><u style="font-size: 11pt; background-color: transparent;">Persistent Area Search and Interdiction</u></p><p class="ql-indent-1"><span style="font-size: 11pt; background-color: transparent; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">The solution provides persistent, low-cost autonomous surveillance and interdiction of defined maritime operating areas, maximizing operational coverage, probability of detection, interdiction effectiveness, and time on station while minimizing daily operating cost, logistics burden, and required personnel. Solutions that deliver greater sustained area coverage and operational effectiveness at lower cost will be evaluated more favorably.</span></p><p class="ql-indent-1"><br></p><p class="ql-indent-1"><u style="font-size: 11pt; background-color: transparent;">UAS System Operations</u></p><p class="ql-indent-1"><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;">Able to carry, launch, control, and employ a minimum of two UAS, one of which must carry a 2kg+ kinetic payload. Solutions should demonstrate reliable integration between the USV, UAS, sensors, and C2 systems. All engagement capability is desired to be capable of remote operation, with appropriate safety measures such that the USV may be recovered and reused. The USV and all embarked UAS assets shall support First Person View (FPV) Beyond Line of Sight (BLOS) operations, enabling operators to maintain positive control of both maritime and airborne assets throughout mission execution. Solutions that support larger onboard drone quantities, higher payload capacity, sortie generation rates, or generate effects against both maritime surface threats and low-altitude airborne threats will be viewed favorably during evaluation. The Government encourages offerors to propose innovative mixes of UAS classes and employment concepts that optimize mission effectiveness. Solutions may combine reusable, attritable, and expendable aircraft of differing payload capacities, ranges, endurance, and operational roles where doing so improves overall system performance.</span></p><p><br></p><p class="ql-indent-1"><u style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;">Mature System</u></p><p class="ql-indent-1"><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;">Solutions must include a complete mission ready USV with integrated drone capability system available for testing and evaluation within </span><strong style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;">29</strong><strong style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(255, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;"> </strong><strong style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;">days of down-selection for Sprint 1</strong><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;">. Solution briefs must address prior operational demonstrations, system maturity, proven integration, command-and-control architecture, and TRL. The Government is seeking production-ready capabilities and is not interested in conceptual designs, developmental efforts, or prototype-only solutions. Offers must demonstrate an established manufacturing capability and active production line for both the USVs and UASs. Solutions demonstrating greater production, scalability and surge capacity will be viewed more favorably during evaluation. Industry partnerships and teaming arrangements that are not sufficiently mature in time for the September evaluation may be considered during subsequent evaluation windows. </span></p><p><br></p><p class="ql-indent-1"><u style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;">Open Architecture and Teaming</u></p><p class="ql-indent-1"><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;">Solutions should leverage market-ready technologies and support modular integration of UAS, sensors, payloads, and software from multiple vendors. The Government encourages teaming arrangements that combine mature USV platforms with proven drone capabilities and other best-of-breed technologies to deliver an integrated, mission-ready solution. Solutions that demonstrate integration and operational employment of multiple drone types from different manufactures will be viewed favorably during evaluation. Open, interoperable architectures that enable rapid integration of new payloads, sensors, and autonomous capabilities over time are highly encouraged.  </span></p><p><br></p><p><strong style="font-family: Lato, sans-serif; font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;">Desired Secondary Attribute(s)</strong></p><p><br></p><p class="ql-indent-1"><u style="font-size: 11pt; background-color: transparent;">Low Burden Logistics</u></p><p class="ql-indent-1"><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;">Able to be moved and launched via standard vehicles without specialized equipment and transportable via common cargo containers such as a forty-foot equivalent unit (FEU), on common cargo aircraft (e.g., C-17 or C-130), and road trailers. Solutions that can launch from unimproved locations or provide additional launch flexibility, i.e. remotely from a container, will be looked upon favorably.</span></p><p class="ql-indent-1"><br></p><p class="ql-indent-1"><u style="font-size: 11pt; background-color: transparent;">Resilient Comms and Localization</u></p><p class="ql-indent-1"><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;">Able to operate in various degrees of denied, disrupted, intermittent and limited (DDIL) conditions. Systems must have resilient communications pathways to operators at various ranges to allow for direct operator supervision and be able to localize in environments where Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) may be denied, degraded or spoofed for indeterminate periods of time.</span></p><p class="ql-indent-1"><br></p><p class="ql-indent-1"><u style="font-size: 11pt; background-color: transparent;">Autonomous Maritime Operations</u><span style="font-size: 11pt; background-color: transparent;"> </span></p><p class="ql-indent-1"><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;">USVs and drones should be able to autonomously navigate to user-defined waypoints, patrol designated areas, loiter on station, autonomously follow or shadow a vessel of interest, and autonomously intercept a noncooperative, maneuvering vessel. Autonomous execution of these functions is desired but not required.</span></p><p class="ql-indent-1"><br></p><p><strong style="font-family: Lato, sans-serif; font-size: 13pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;">Additional Evaluation Criteria</strong></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;">Details must be provided in the solution proposal. These additional elements will be evaluated during proposal review, down-selection gates, and live testing:</span></p><p><br></p><table class="ql-table-blob" style="border-width: medium; border-style: none; Standalone submissions must provide sufficient interface documentation to support future integration. </span></p><p><br></p><p><span style="font-size: 11pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); background-color: transparent;">Offerors may propose multiple USV/UAS variants or platform mixes within a single submission. Offerers are encouraged to propose multiple UAS employment concepts where different configurations optimize different operational tradeoffs (i.e. magazine depth, range, payload capacity, persistence, or cost-per-effect).</span></p><p><br></p><p><strong style="font-size: 11pt; Norman serves as the acting Portfolio Director for the Defense Innovation Unit’s (DIU) Emerging Technology Portfolio. In this role, he accelerates the transition of commercial and dual-use technologies into operational capabilities for the Department of War (DoW). He works closely with DoW stakeholders and industry partners to shape portfolio strategy, launch high-impact projects, and drive outcomes from prototype\nthrough fielding and scale.\n\nHis portfolio spans hypersonics, quantum sensing, microelectronics, directed energy, and any other technologies that create strategic overmatch. Kyle focuses on aligning commercially viable innovation with\npriority efforts to ensure the Department maintains a decisive lead in emerging domains. He regularly engages with startups, established firms, investors, and research organizations to assess technical maturity, scalability, and pathways to operational adoption.\n\nKyle brings more than 20 years of experience in senior program management, systems engineering, and strategic technology integration within the DoD. Prior to joining DIU, he led a portfolio at the Office of Naval\nResearch with and annual budget in excess $250M. He has served in senior, policy, advisory, and requirements roles supporting Fleet, Joint, and interagency missions. He holds an M.S. in Systems Engineering from the Naval Postgraduate School and a B.S. in Chemical Engineering (Honors).",nodeType:a}],nodeType:c}],nodeType:q},office:kT,headshot:{metadata:{tags:[],concepts:[]},sys:{space:{sys:{type:b,linkType:d,id:e}},id:"DDjWZipJeSCXekcgf6cMu",type:m,createdAt:"2026-05-29T16:26:25.316Z",updatedAt:"2026-05-29T16:27:38.681Z",environment:{sys:{id:f,type:b,linkType:g}},publishedVersion:M,revision:s,locale:h},fields:{title:"Kyle Norman headshot",description:i,file:{url:"\u002F\u002Fimages.ctfassets.net\u002F3nanhbfkr0pc\u002FDDjWZipJeSCXekcgf6cMu\u002Fc4fad780ae2f8e2d3f284df7ccd828df\u002FKyle_norman__1_.jpg",details:{size:523922,image:{width:2846,height:3557}},fileName:"Kyle_norman (1).jpg",contentType:w}}},group:bV}},{metadata:{tags:[],concepts:[]},sys:{space:{sys:{type:b,linkType:d,id:e}},id:"22G5eh15tEf0klVyolsmoG",type:j,createdAt:"2022-11-28T19:29:51.205Z",updatedAt:"2024-07-08T20:43:58.961Z",environment:{sys:{id:f,type:b,linkType:g}},publishedVersion:ap,revision:y,contentType:{sys:{type:b,linkType:k,id:bw}},locale:h},fields:{fullName:aaT,lastName:"Higier",slug:"dr-andrew-higier",titleRank:"Director, Energy Portfolio",bio:{nodeType:q,data:{},content:[{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:i,marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:o,data:{uri:"https:\u002F\u002Fimages.ctfassets.net\u002F3nanhbfkr0pc\u002F1uwGIedl5GeJm8b3bPAbf4\u002Fd6ebd2352c72c61071d10e79c49fa9e2\u002FHigier_Andrew_adobe_express.jpeg"},content:[{nodeType:a,value:z$,marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:a,value:i,marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Dr. Andrew Higier serves as the Director of the Energy Portfolio at the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU). The Energy Portfolio is focused on two primary lines of effort: Installation Resilience and Operational Energy.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Dr. Higier has spent over a decade focused on bringing innovative technologies to the warfighter. The portfolio’s mission is to accelerate the transition of commercial innovation and technology to government and defense personnel, covering a wide area of problem sets from safety and survivability, training and simulation, to prevention and treatment of combat injuries. ",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Prior to joining DIU, Christian served in several roles within the military science and technology (S&T) community, most recently as the Chief Scientist for Detection and Diagnostics within the ChemBio Defense Program, and as the U.S. S&T representative for a collaborative agreement between the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia. With 15 years of government service, Christian is a strong advocate for thinking beyond the conventional requirements process and delivering new technologies that can help our warfighters succeed and survive.   ",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Christian received his BS in chemistry from the University of Tennessee at Martin and his PhD in analytical chemistry from Ohio University before completing postdoctoral studies at the FBI’s Research Unit. He is a lifelong student, most recently attending business venture courses at the Berkeley Haas school. Christian’s side gigs include parachute rigging and sports photography. ",marks:[],data:{}}]}]},office:os,headshot:{metadata:{tags:[],concepts:[]},sys:{space:{sys:{type:b,linkType:d,id:e}},id:"Z09eUMZ5sUZEhB2709FY0",type:m,createdAt:"2020-09-29T20:17:50.839Z",updatedAt:"2025-07-01T12:08:09.280Z",environment:{sys:{id:f,type:b,linkType:g}},publishedVersion:bn,revision:M,locale:h},fields:{title:"Christian Whitchurch Headshot",file:{url:"\u002F\u002Fimages.ctfassets.net\u002F3nanhbfkr0pc\u002FZ09eUMZ5sUZEhB2709FY0\u002F46c28b5c50530ddd0b0722e0a46f81c9\u002FWhitchurch__Christian_03_adobe_express__1_.jpeg",details:{size:77105,image:{width:fT,height:jk}},fileName:"Whitchurch  Christian 03_adobe_express (1).jpeg",contentType:w}}},group:bV}},{metadata:{tags:[],concepts:[]},sys:{space:{sys:{type:b,linkType:d,id:e}},id:"6a3RCZ2beDgRnrzuTdCQwP",type:j,createdAt:"2019-12-05T20:20:10.889Z",updatedAt:"2026-04-24T18:26:19.289Z",environment:{sys:{id:f,type:b,linkType:g}},publishedVersion:144,revision:aS,contentType:{sys:{type:b,linkType:k,id:bw}},locale:h},fields:{fullName:aaW,lastName:"Butow",slug:"Steven-Butow",titleRank:"Senior Advisor to the Director",bio:{data:{},content:[{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[],value:i,nodeType:a},{data:{uri:"https:\u002F\u002Fimages.ctfassets.net\u002F3nanhbfkr0pc\u002F29rMSHPs1lH30yABKEMcwu\u002Fbd67d7ede1c2aed42eef399a247d67dc\u002FMG_Steven_Butow_8x10.jpeg"},content:[{data:{},marks:[],value:z$,nodeType:a}],nodeType:o},{data:{},marks:[],value:i,nodeType:a}],nodeType:c},{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[],value:"Steve “Bucky” Butow is the Director, Space Portfolio of the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU), Office of the Secretary of Defense.",nodeType:a}],nodeType:c},{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[],value:"General Butow joined the team in 2015 as an early plank owner when DIU was known as the Defense Innovation Unit Experimental (DIUx).  He initially served as  West Coast Military Lead and helped establish the organization’s operating locations in Silicon Valley, California; Boston, Massachusetts; and Austin, Texas.  In 2016, he was was selected as DIU’s first Space Portfolio Director.  Upon promotion to brigadier general, Butow continued this role at DIU as a DoD civilian.",nodeType:a}],nodeType:c},{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[],value:"General Butow continues to serve as the Commander of the California Air National Guard in a dual Title 10\u002F32 status where he leads 4,900 Airmen assigned to five wings and a headquarters staff performing air, space and cyber operations as part of the Total Air Force.  He commanded the 129th Rescue Wing at Moffett Field, CA, from 2011 to 2014.",nodeType:a}],nodeType:c},{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[],value:"General Butow’s previous Title 10 leadership assignments include Deputy Director of the Joint Search and Rescue Center for U.S. Central Command in 2005, and as Chief of Personnel Recovery for U.S. Air Forces Central in 2007 supporting Operations IRAQI and ENDURING FREEDOM.  Prior to joining DIU, Butow was the Vice Chief of the Joint Staff, California Military Department with responsibilities including cybersecurity, incident awareness and innovation. He has deployed ten times to support combat and contingency operations across Southwest Asia, the Middle East, the Horn of Africa and other global locations.  General Butow has more than 3,500 flying hours in T-37, T-38, C-130, HC-130 and MC-130P aircraft. ",nodeType:a}],nodeType:c},{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[],value:"Butow graduated from San Jose State University with a B.A. in Physics & Astronomy and earned a M.S. in Management with specialization in Air and Space Strategic Studies from the University of Maryland. ",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"What is AVO?",marks:[{type:l}],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:aP,marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"The Autonomous Vehicle Orchestrator (AVO) is software that lets a human operator control autonomous vehicles using various forms of input. Every step is logged for visibility and control over the system.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"What role does Artificial Intelligence (AI) play?",marks:[{type:l}],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:aP,marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"AI is used to normalize the user command & consider environmental factors to select an instruction. If validation fails, the action is blocked. The system fails closed – meaning any ambiguity, validation error, or unsafe condition blocks execution. Additionally, AVO is designed so that operators have full visibility and insight into the system and can intervene or stop operations at any point. Humans remain in-the-loop. ",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"What can the system actually instruct vehicles to do?",marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"The allowed actions are constrained to a set of existing asset capabilities. year, the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) celebrated its seventh year of accelerating commercial technology adoption across the Department of Defense (DoD). Launched as an experiment in 2015, DIU is now a proven business model for prototyping and acquiring leading-edge technology. In Fiscal Year (FY) 2022, DIU successfully transitioned 17 technology solutions to defense and civilian agency end-users, equating to $1.3B in contract award ceiling. The volume of transitions in FY 2022 is also the greatest we have seen in a single fiscal year, and more than double the eight transitions we saw in FY 2021.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"The core of DIU operations continues to be fueled by our Commercial Solutions Opening process leveraging the Other Transaction “OT” authority, and a commitment to being a “fast follower” of commercial technology. We owe much of where we are today as an organization to his hard work and vision. ",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"As we move further along into FY 2023, DIU remains dedicated to accelerating commercial solutions to our DoD and U.S. government partners, strengthening our national security innovation base by lowering the barriers to entry and providing recurring revenue to non-traditional companies. The result is a set of Responsible AI Guidelines that are informed by DIU’s practical experience, but also draw upon best practices from government, non-profit, academic, and industry partners. ",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"DIU will continue collaborating with experts and stakeholders from government, industry, academia, and civil society to further develop the RAI Guidelines. Powered by Talent: Joshua Zike",body:{nodeType:q,data:{},content:[{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Joshua Zike is an active duty U.S. Coast Guard officer who serves as the senior service lead  to DIU and is a  program manager within the autonomy portfolio. Prior to joining DIU in the summer of 2023, he was the Commanding Officer of the USCG Cutter ELM (WLB 204), which is homeported in Astoria, Oregon, from 2020-2023. He is a career cutterman with the USCG and was the Commanding Officer of the of the USCGC NEAH BAY (WTGB 105) from 2014-2017, and has served onboard the USCGC BISCAYNE BAY (WTGB 104) and USCGC ASPEN (WLB 208). He is a 2005 graduate of the U.S. Coast Guard Academy.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:i,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:ai$,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"I want to propel the U.S. Coast Guard and the military forward by leveraging the best-of-breed commercial dual-use technology to solve emerging capability and operational gaps. I am drawn to DIU’s mission and the opportunity to work with  non-traditional defense contractors and execute innovative prototype projects with a fast-paced team.\n",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"I’ve also found out that working with DIU meant working with a whole team of people looking for ways to get to yes - which is a big culture shift from previous experiences.  \n",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"What problem are you currently working to solve \u002F what project?",marks:[{type:l}],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:Q,marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"The autonomy portfolio is working with the U.S. Navy to ensure they can autonomously monitor and secure  hundreds of miles of contested waterspace through the Production-Ready, Inexpensive, Maritime Expeditionary (PRIME) Small Unmanned Surface Vehicle (sUSV) and Collaborative Intercept Capability project.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Our AMERV project is supporting the USN's Explosive Ordnance Disposal  community, and I’m also assisting with a Wireless Crew project that is being led by Sam Amedia in DIU’s Human Systems portfolio with the Coast Guard as the sole mission partner.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"What are you currently inspired by in your work at DIU?",marks:[{type:l}],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:aP,marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"I'm driven by a desire to make things better for those out in the field, on the water, or in the skies. Service members face various operational challenges and difficulties that can be solved by existing commercial dual-use technology - and delivering these solutions to them motivates me to continue pushing forward every day.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"What are you currently reading\u002F recommend - or - what podcast are you listening to\u002F recommend, and why?",marks:[{type:l}],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:aP,marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"For anyone new to the innovation and technology space, the In-Q-Tel podcast is a great way to get  exposed to some emerging defense tech. From a broader leadership standpoint, I also listen to the Craig Groeschel Leadership podcast regularly, which helps keep me grounded. I'm currently reading \"The End of the World is Just the Beginning\" by Peter Zeihan and it's a very interesting perspective on the geopolitical shift that is occurring right now across the globe, and how the U.S.'s changing global maritime strategy has such a broad impact on everything.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"What are you currently celebrating?",marks:[{type:l}],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:aP,marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"We closed the solicitation for the PRIME sUSV project before the DIU Tech Summit: Deploying & Scaling Autonomy for Strategic Impact hosted at DIU Headquarters in Mountain View, CA.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"A three year effort to update and align Coast Guard Other Transaction Authorities to be on par with the DOD, will be realized pending the the passing of a full year FY24 appropriations bill. Once this occurs, the CG is standing by to issue internal policy on executing OTs within the Coast Guard. Progress here has been the result of extensive effort with the CG's Legislative Affairs team and DIU’s prior CG liaison, Nordy, who laid out the groundwork to make this possible.",marks:[],data:{}}]}]}}}],ctaImage:{metadata:{tags:[],concepts:[]},sys:{space:{sys:{type:b,linkType:d,id:e}},id:"167kwVaFqeKGAF2OSRI74s",type:m,createdAt:"2024-02-22T16:08:39.724Z",updatedAt:"2024-02-22T16:08:57.424Z",environment:{sys:{id:f,type:b,linkType:g}},publishedVersion:M,revision:s,locale:h},fields:{title:"Powered published on October 20, 2022",marks:[{type:A}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Brian “Ponch” Rivera is the co-creator of The Flow System™, founder and CEO of AGLX Consulting, co-founder and co-owner of AGLX Holdings, and a founding member of The Flow Consortium.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"He is the co-author of a FORBES-noted Top Ten Mind-Opening Business book for 2020, ",marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:"The Flow System-The Evolution of Agile and Lean Thinking in an Age of Complexity",marks:[{type:A}],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:".  He is an Amazon International Best Selling author for his work on ",marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:"Strength and Gratitude",marks:[{type:A}],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:" and is currently working on his fourth book focused on connecting mental health and adaptive performance.. In 2020, prior to the pandemic, he delivered his TEDx talk, ",marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:"Design for Flow",marks:[{type:A}],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:" in Budapest, Hungary following an  engagement with NATO leaders where he spoke on  complexity thinking and flow.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"He is the co-creator of High-Performance Teaming and the creator of ZONEFIVE—a behavioral marker system that objectively measures team effectiveness. ",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"You can learn more about Ponch’s work on several recent  podcasts including the Baptist Medical System’s Connecting the Dots Podcast,  The Salience Podcast, and The Economics for Business Podcast. ",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Ponch, his callsign from naval aviation, served on active duty for 16 years before transferring to the Navy Reserve and now wears the rank of CAPTAIN as a part-time member of the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU).",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"As an entrepreneur, Ponch leverages the leadership, teamwork, and lessons he learned throughout his diverse military career and civilian experience to help individuals and organizations create the agility, resilience, and safety they need to survive and thrive in this turbulent world. He is an avid options trader and is currently involved in an upcoming mental health documentary that features his work on flow and human performance.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:oK,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Our nation needs the Department of Defense (DoD) to be agile and innovative or we risk losing the ability to survive and thrive on our own terms. DIU exists to solve these problems through acting as a broker with the commercial sector and creating the conditions for innovation to emerge.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Having served on active duty for 16 years and as a Government Service employee, I experienced what it is like to work around the system in a time of crisis, how  bureaucracy and ordered processes stifle innovation,  and how acquisition delays ensure our warfighters get “yesterday’s technology, tomorrow!”  This is unacceptable but is currently the norm.  ",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"I couldn’t take the pain; so I left active duty and began working full-time in the government to become an Agile coach.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"While working in industry, I learned that many of today’s Agile software development and Lean manufacturing practices were influenced by lessons from the military. For example, Scrum is influenced by the observe–orient–decide–act (OODA) loop of fighter aviation, as is The Lean Startup concept. Moreover, agility is an outcome of better quality OODA loops; similarly, innovation and safety are emergent properties of our interactions (better OODA loops). There are many more connections I can make but I think I should save those discussions for a later time. My point: The DoD knows how to innovate and deliver, we just added too much order to our complex system.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"In 2018 I was working with Jeff Sutherland, the co-creator of Scrum when I was hand-picked to engage with industry and academia to help the U.S. Navy identify how to develop high-performance teams and leaders, change culture, improve safety, and capture leading indicators. It was the leading indicator work from DARPA and Dave Snowden that led me to DIU. I found out that the DIU director used a paradigm-shifting sensemaking tool to capture current culture. I knew then that I wanted to be part of this new organization.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:sG,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"So far, my favorite DIU experience was working with a few of the National Security Innovation Network directors and DIU staff to help build strategic situational awareness using a mapping technique known as Wardley Mapping. The idea is we need to build a shared understanding of the landscape that includes the needs of users, customers, and stakeholders before we can develop a cohesive strategy.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:Cw,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Before I share my answer, I want to share a mantra and a trinity that I think many people in the business of defense forget.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Mantra: “Machines don’t fight wars, people do, and they use their minds.”",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Trinity: People first, ideas second, and things (technology) third.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Col. John Boyd, a real DoD maverick and innovator, promoted this mantra and trinity around the Pentagon in the 70s and 80s yet, today, it seems our defense ecosystem favors machines and technology over people. I think this is wrong!",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"We live in an era where 17-22 veterans, former warriors, take their lives each day. In 2021, 500 service members took their own lives. The ratio of suicides among active-duty personnel and veterans to deaths from military operations since 9-11 is four to one. Suicide is a visible outcome of the often invisible mental health challenges associated with serving our country. These challenges include post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), traumatic brain injury (TBI), anxiety, depression, and addiction.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Mental health is the number one DoD problem I would tackle as there are many commercial solutions that could be used immediately. The sooner we can solve the mental health crisis inside our ranks, the sooner our nation can heal from its unprecedented mental health crisis associated with the pandemic and our rapidly changing world. To make this connection stronger, I want to wrap this section up with a quote from Thích Nhất Hạnh:",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"“Veterans are the light at the tip of the candle, illuminating the way for the whole nation. If veterans can achieve awareness, transformation, understanding, and peace, they can share with the rest of society the realities of war. And they can teach us how to make peace with ourselves and each other, so we never have to use violence to resolve conflicts again.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:aP,marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:oL,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"I’m very excited about any biotech, entheogenic medicine, or human performance activity that (1) enables neural networks in the brain to change through growth and reorganization (neuroplasticity) and\u002For (2) promotes the growth of new neurons in the brain (neurogenesis).",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"On the biotech side, sensory substitution (peripheral) devices such as wearable wristbands that capture sound and convert them to patterns of vibration on the skin for neurons in the brain to make new connections show tons of promise for helping the hearing impaired.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Through peripheral devices and the natural neuroplasticity process, I think there is an opportunity to rewire the brain so we can experience our umwelt (surrounding world) in ways that go beyond our normal senses—something that may provide our warriors an edge on the battlefield.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"More importantly, when our warriors return from the battlefield, we must leverage what we know about neuroplasticity and neurogenesis to help our brothers and sisters deal with post-traumatic disorders associated with military service. To be clear, I’m talking about how we can tackle the biggest problem in the Department of Defense: mental health—this includes PTSD, TBI, anxiety, addiction, and stress.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"There are two ways the commercial sector is more advanced than the DoD when it comes to tackling the growing mental health crisis. The first is an outside-in bottom-up approach that includes the medically supervised use of entheogens or psychedelics. The second is a top-down inside-out approach to include breathing exercises, yoga, mindfulness, and meditation. This second approach has some traction inside the DoD, so I will skip details of that here.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:sH,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:" I’m reading five books at the moment, all of them are interconnected and related to mental health and adaptive performance.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:J,data:{},content:[{nodeType:n,data:{},content:[{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"An Immense World ",marks:[{type:A}],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:"by Ed Yong, a book on how animals sense the world around them and was recommended to me by Anil Seth, author of ",marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:ajI,marks:[{type:A}],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:"(",marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:ajI,marks:[{type:A}],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:"is a MUST READ)",marks:[],data:{}}]}]},{nodeType:n,data:{},content:[{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Behave: The Biology of Humans at our Best and Worst by  Robert Sapolsky",marks:[{type:A}],data:{}}]}]},{nodeType:n,data:{},content:[{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Gödel, Escher, Bach: An Eternal Golden Braid ",marks:[{type:A}],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:"by Douglas Hoftstadter",marks:[],data:{}}]}]},{nodeType:n,data:{},content:[{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"The Quantum Revelation ",marks:[{type:A}],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:"by Paul Levy",marks:[],data:{}}]}]}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"The fifth book is",marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:" Lean Leadership Basics",marks:[{type:A}],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:" by my friend and mentor, Charlie Protzman. Charlie is a Shingo Prize-winning author and a few years ago I worked with him on how to incorporate leadership and teamwork lessons from fighter aviation and the military into Lean. If you are looking for ways to improve manufacturing or understand Lean, Charlie’s book is a must read.",marks:[],data:{}}]}]}}}]}},{metadata:{tags:[],concepts:[]},sys:{space:{sys:{type:b,linkType:d,id:e}},id:"5NTDV6hbtZthOxMUPd72nI",type:j,createdAt:"2023-05-02T15:37:01.584Z",updatedAt:"2023-08-08T15:26:07.554Z",environment:{sys:{id:f,type:b,linkType:g}},publishedVersion:aC,revision:s,contentType:{sys:{type:b,linkType:k,id:S}},locale:h},fields:{title:ajJ,slug:"powered-by-talent-cherissa-tamayori",metaTitle:"Powered by Talent: Cherissa Tamayori | DIU",metaSocialShareImage:{metadata:{tags:[],concepts:[]},sys:{space:{sys:{type:b,linkType:d,id:e}},id:"2GXsP2vM4AINzdBX39LIP1",type:m,createdAt:"2023-03-23T15:49:05.539Z",updatedAt:"2023-05-02T15:36:54.915Z",environment:{sys:{id:f,type:b,linkType:g}},publishedVersion:I,revision:s,locale:h},fields:{title:"Powered by Talent - Cherissa Tamayori (Body)",body:{nodeType:q,data:{},content:[{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Originally published November 30, 2021",marks:[{type:A}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Cherissa Tamayori is the Director of Acquisition and Senior Contracting Official for the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU). She  manages DIU’s acquisition functions and leads a team of senior acquisition professionals leveraging the use of the Other Transaction Authority to accelerate the adoption of commercial technology within the DoD.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Prior to joining DIU, Cherissa served as a contracting officer in the Navy where she managed multi-billion dollar contract portfolios for various undersea systems programs. As a contract specialist, she negotiated and administered complex shipbuilding procurements including the refueling, overhaul, and modernization of a nuclear-powered aircraft carrier and the design and construction of auxiliary ships and patrol boats. In addition to these roles, Cherissa has served in various contracting positions within the Navy.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:oK,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"The majority of my career has been in public service. I have always been interested in learning from commercial sector leaders--how these entities operate, what their interests are, how decisions are made -- so the DoD can be a better partner.  The diversity of experiences, from operational to commercial, within DIU allows us to learn from and collaborate with a wide range of technical experts, an opportunity that is rarely seen in government acquisition offices.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:sG,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:abo,marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:aP,marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:oL,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Lately, I’m excited about DIU’s new ",marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:o,data:{uri:Cx},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Responsible Artificial Intelligence (RAI) guidance",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:a,value:". AI is a powerful and ever-evolving tool; like any technology, however, it can result in unintended consequences if left unchecked. As a buyer of AI technology, the government needs to proactively address ethical concerns, and I believe the RAI report is going to help the program management and acquisition communities do just that!",marks:[],data:{}}]}]}}}]}},{metadata:{tags:[],concepts:[]},sys:{space:{sys:{type:b,linkType:d,id:e}},id:"6ccYkOM64SfQWBMUdypre",type:j,createdAt:"2023-05-02T15:39:56.236Z",updatedAt:"2023-08-08T15:25:39.359Z",environment:{sys:{id:f,type:b,linkType:g}},publishedVersion:ab,revision:s,contentType:{sys:{type:b,linkType:k,id:S}},locale:h},fields:{title:ajM,slug:"powered-by-talent-jared-dunnmon",metaTitle:ajN,metaSocialShareImage:{metadata:{tags:[],concepts:[]},sys:{space:{sys:{type:b,linkType:d,id:e}},id:"3V1VeEPeyqRMGgYQ0YvK4M",type:m,createdAt:"2023-03-23T15:33:05.827Z",updatedAt:"2023-05-02T15:39:52.394Z",environment:{sys:{id:f,type:b,linkType:g}},publishedVersion:I,revision:s,locale:h},fields:{title:"Powered by Talent - Jared Dunnmon - Body",body:{nodeType:q,data:{},content:[{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"February 22, 2022",marks:[{type:A}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Dr. Jared Dunnmon is the Technical Director for Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Machine Learning (ML) at the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU). In this role, he brings a technical perspective to problem curation, vendor sourcing and evaluation, and project execution. Prior to DIU, Jared was an Intelligence Community Postdoctoral Fellow in Computer Science at Stanford University, where he was advised by Prof. Chris Ré. His research interests focus on combining heterogeneous data modalities, machine learning, and human domain expertise to inform and improve decision making around such topics as human health, energy & environment, and geopolitical stability. Jared holds a PhD from Stanford University (2017), a B.S. from Duke University, and both an MSc. in Mathematical Modeling and Scientific Computing and an M.B.A. from Oxford, where he studied as a Rhodes Scholar.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:oK,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"I chose to move to DIU from a successful startup because it offered a unique opportunity to combine my technical skillset and industry experience in support of national security. I was also attracted by the incredible team of folks from industry, technology, and government, from whom I can learn an amazing amount every day.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:sG,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"This is a really hard question – I love what I do every day. If I had to choose, my favorite experience was making the trip to Guam to deploy an augmented reality microscope that could help the pathology team at the Naval Medical Hospital more rapidly identify cancer. It is rare that one gets to see a project from development through deployment, and in this case it was particularly satisfying to be able to observe exactly how the cutting edge technology involved in this project could be used to improve medical care in low-resource environments.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"If you could solve any Department of Defense (DoD) problem tomorrow, no matter how big, what would you tackle and why? ",marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Changing the budget process such that DoD can more rapidly integrate emerging technologies into its operations. At present, when we have a successful prototype that was built with *research* funding, it can take years before the *sustainment* funding is allocated, leaving potentially transformational technologies on the sidelines. We have to move at the speed of relevance, and the funding cycle is a major blocker. We continue to make this case at DIU and find ways to move the ball forward.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:oL,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"One of the most exciting parts of working at DIU is that, while I formally sit on the AI portfolio, I work very closely with folks in our other portfolios like Space, Energy, Cyber, Human Systems, and Autonomy. On the AI front, I’m particularly excited about leveraging knowledge graphs to drive how we think about people, places, and things, and how we combine continually improving approaches to MLOps with low-power edge computing hardware to change the way that we deploy AI systems. Outside of AI, I am particularly bullish on leveraging technologies like small remote sensing satellites, renewable energy systems, and advanced manufacturing to simultaneously improve operational capability, enhance resilience to climate change, and reduce the public sector carbon emission footprint. ",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:sH,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Over the holidays, I managed to catch up on most of the International Conference on Learning Representations papers that had been on my reading list. I just finished ",marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:"Aftershocks",marks:[{type:A}],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:" by Colin Kahl and Thomas Wright, an excellent book about the effect that the pandemic has had and will continue to have on geopolitics. I’m just getting started on ",marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:"The Dark Forest",marks:[{type:A}],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:" by Liu Cixin (the sequel to the Three-Body Problem).",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:Cy,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"In my role as Technical Director for AI, I have anywhere from 10-15 individual projects that I am tracking at any one time. Applications range from predictive maintenance (with the Air Force) to knowledge graph construction (with the intelligence community) to combatting illegal fishing with computer vision (with the U.S. Coast Guard), and I have spent a lot of time on this last one – including a good number of coding hours – via the ",marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:o,data:{uri:ahh},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"xView3 machine learning prize challenge",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:a,value:" that just concluded this month. At a higher level, I also try to address common issues across our programs and provide some strategic direction for the type of problems we spend our time working on. In November, for instance, we released the ",marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:o,data:{uri:"https:\u002F\u002Fwww.diu.mil\u002Flatest\u002Fdiu-operationalizes-responsible-ai-guidelines-in-practice"},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"DIU Responsible AI Guidelines",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:a,value:", which represented nearly a year and a half of work to provide actionable guidance on how DIU aims to operationalize the DoD AI Ethical Principles. I am also currently working to put forth an architecture for MLOps within the DoD that strategically leverages the latest commercial technology to improve the efficacy with which DoD can rapidly iterate on machine learning models it aims to deploy.",marks:[],data:{}}]}]},classes:Cz}}]}},{metadata:{tags:[],concepts:[]},sys:{space:{sys:{type:b,linkType:d,id:e}},id:"6bncTzKH99Uyd9LVqNsII9",type:j,createdAt:"2023-05-02T15:42:54.373Z",updatedAt:"2023-08-08T15:25:27.621Z",environment:{sys:{id:f,type:b,linkType:g}},publishedVersion:aA,revision:s,contentType:{sys:{type:b,linkType:k,id:S}},locale:h},fields:{title:ajQ,slug:"powered-by-talent-kim-guedry",metaTitle:ajN,metaSocialShareImage:{metadata:{tags:[],concepts:[]},sys:{space:{sys:{type:b,linkType:d,id:e}},id:"44KDLOsoO5k6NJwx4aGWWT",type:m,createdAt:"2023-03-22T13:25:19.116Z",updatedAt:"2023-05-02T15:42:51.122Z",environment:{sys:{id:f,type:b,linkType:g}},publishedVersion:I,revision:s,locale:h},fields:{title:"#PoweredbyTalent_Guedry",description:i,file:{url:"\u002F\u002Fimages.ctfassets.net\u002F3nanhbfkr0pc\u002F44KDLOsoO5k6NJwx4aGWWT\u002Fbec2011af3b3fd750a6828e905baf104\u002FMy_project__11___1_.jpg",details:{size:184315,image:{width:r,height:x}},fileName:"My 2022",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"CAPT Kim Guedry is the Director of the Joint Reserve Detachment (JRD) at the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU). In this role, she brings more than 23 years of military experience across a wide spectrum of capacities. ",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"While on active duty, Kim’s roles ranged from Commanding Officer of a Coast Guard cutter (ship) to Command Duty Officer in the Service’s busiest command center. Following her transition to the reserves, Kim held various liaison positions in the Department of Defense (DoD) and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including her role as a Coast Guard Emergency Preparedness Liaison Officer to FEMA. In her role as Director of JRD, she provides specialty reserve personnel from across the Services in direct support of DIU’s six portfolios, while dual-hatting as the Service lead for the U.S. Coast Guard’s reserve efforts at DIU.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"As a civilian, Kim co-founded two startups, one in the AgTech industry and one in business continuity consulting. Kim is currently the Director of Business Operations at Lumen Technologies, a Fortune 200 tech company, where she also serves as Chief of Staff in the North America Field Operations organization. ",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Kim is a proud ",marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:o,data:{uri:"https:\u002F\u002Fuscga.edu\u002F"},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"U.S. Coast Guard Academy",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:a,value:" graduate, a George W. Bush Institute and National Defense University scholar, and she earned her MBA with a specialty in Human Resources Management while on active duty.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:oK,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Throughout my professional career, both in and out of the military, I have been attracted to new or slightly ambiguous roles. I learned of DIU in its infancy through a start-up I co-founded, and an opportunity to be a part of the DIU team came in 2020 when the Coast Guard created a number of positions at DIU. It seemed to be the perfect fit given my previous DoD and DHS liaison roles, my strong interest in the diversity of the six technology portfolios, my start-up background, as well as my leadership roles in the tech industry. Moreover, the opportunity to work in an innovative environment drew me in.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"What is your favorite DIU experience thus far?",marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"That’s easy—the people. DIU has the most incredible team of people I have ever worked with. From humility to humor, intelligence to insightfulness, and passion to purpose; I am in awe of the capabilities of each and every one of the DIU team members. Regardless of their roots in industry, technology, government, or academia, this team shares, learns, and does as one. It is both a joy and inspiration to be a part of such a grounded and driven team, working together for a purpose greater than their own.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:Cw,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Steve Blank recently shared with our DIU team the following, “The DoD (I would fold DHS in here) is a world-class organization, filled with world-class people but built for a world that no longer exists.” If I could solve anything with the wave of a magic wand, it would be the shift to a fully-innovative culture.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"What does that mean? First, the good news. I have little doubt that when it comes to the “want to” of having an innovative culture, most are all-in; however, implementation gets sticky. Second, in order for that implementation to happen, the end-to-end process requires both extensive journey-mapping at all levels and policy rewrites to ensure items like the budget process help, not hinder, an innovative environment. Finally, like any culture shift, it will take time. However, in my opinion, the phrase “well, that’s how we’ve always done it” needs to be extracted from DoD and the U.S. Government vocabulary. From the newest member on a team to the most seasoned, healthy curiosity into doing something safer, cheaper, smarter, or faster should be a table stakes question.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Those close to me know that I cannot stand the often-used phrase, “It is what it is.” No! Regardless of what “it” is, if you don’t like it, it’s no longer working, either change it or change your view of it, but don’t just accept it. Both our personal and professional lives are filled with hundreds of choices, big and small, each day—we allocate our finite resources (time, people, funding) to our priorities and what is most important. I would make an innovative culture one of those choices.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:oL,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"I feel like this is a trick question—that’s the glory of DIU! The opportunities are near endless. What’s emerging right now and what is a mere thought, has the potential to land in the hands of our military members and make their lives and our nation safer, stronger, or more efficient and effective. I used to describe DIU as the place where the question “Wouldn’t it be cool if ABC could do XYZ?” is being worked on every single day.   ",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:sH,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"I am a self-proclaimed leadership and management book junkie. No one book is the “silver bullet” and I rarely re-read books. However, there are two “oldies but goodies” that I am currently re-reading, Ben and Kelly Decker’s ",marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:"Communicate to Influence: How to Inspire Your Audience to Action",marks:[{type:A}],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:" and Milo O. Frank’s ",marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:"How to Get Your Point Across in 30 Seconds or Less",marks:[{type:A}],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:". Effective communication is key - it’s something I don’t think I will ever be settled with.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"\n ",marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:Cy,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Since joining DIU, my efforts have primarily been from a Service lead perspective. While we’ve explored initiatives in each portfolio (yes, even the Space portfolio), two that are furthest developed from a Coast Guard perspective are housed in the Artificial Intelligence\u002FMachine Learning (AI\u002FML) portfolio, namely Wireless Crew and xView3.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:" Supporting our active duty DIU Coast Guardsman (CDR Mike “Nordy” Nordhausen), Wireless Crew goes after an age-old problem with respect to fleet—wide Boat Crew Communications Systems (BCSS). We believe that using a commercial market solution and our DIU process will buy down risk and find a communication solution for our boats that is reliable, strong, useful, and comfortable for our crews. Furthermore, this solution is exciting in that it marks the first use of Other Transaction (OTs) funding by the Coast Guard. This  will enable the Coast Guard to set a precedent and be flexible enough to find the right solutions to solve compelling and long-standing challenges like those with our current communications platforms.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Also, while there is still some work to be done from a training perspective, our xView3 project adds capability to our Service’s counter Illegal, Unreported, and Unregulated (IUU) fishing challenge. As I step into the Director of the JRD role, I am excited to continue learning and gaining additional insight into more of the amazing projects that the collective DIU is working on all the while enabling reservists to play an active role in that development and progress.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"[Some kind of CTA\u002FKicker here (although we do have the sign up widget at the end of the page...]",marks:[{type:l},{type:A}],data:{}}]}]},classes:Cz}}]}},{metadata:{tags:[],concepts:[]},sys:{space:{sys:{type:b,linkType:d,id:e}},id:"7ccsYxFhU7H4eUd34fjSfe",type:j,createdAt:"2023-05-02T15:45:26.887Z",updatedAt:"2023-08-08T15:25:19.173Z",environment:{sys:{id:f,type:b,linkType:g}},publishedVersion:ah,revision:s,contentType:{sys:{type:b,linkType:k,id:S}},locale:h},fields:{title:ajR,slug:ajS,metaTitle:"Powered by Talent - Rogan Shimmin - Body",body:{nodeType:q,data:{},content:[{nodeType:G,data:{target:{metadata:{tags:[],concepts:[]},sys:{space:{sys:{type:b,linkType:d,id:e}},id:ajT,type:m,createdAt:ajU,updatedAt:ajV,environment:{sys:{id:f,type:b,linkType:g}},publishedVersion:I,revision:s,locale:h},fields:{title:ajW,description:i,file:{url:ajX,details:{size:ajY,image:{width:r,height:x}},fileName:ajZ,contentType:w}}}},content:[]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"January 5, 2022",marks:[{type:A}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Rogan Shimmin is a Technical Program Manager and Senior Engineer within DIU’s  Space Portfolio. Prior to joining DIU, Rogan worked at NASA Johnson Space Center performing mission safety analysis for the Orion space capsule. Rogan also spent time at NASA’s Ames Research Center where he led a small satellite team. In his spare time Rogan is a rescue combat systems officer for the 129th Rescue Wing at Moffett Field, California. Rogan was recently invited to participate in the second round of astronaut selection for the European Space Agency. He is eagerly awaiting the results.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:$,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:oK,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"Through my experience working on government-owned, government-operated systems at NASA, I quickly learned that there are certain expectations we have for commercial solutions that are somehow missing within government development—the most obvious example being intuitive and responsive user interfaces. I was frustrated by the tendency within government technology research programs to spend years producing a widget, only to then put that widget on a shelf to gather dust. In contrast, commercial solutions are driven by a commercial demand, which propels them across the valley of death and into production. DIU presented an opportunity for me to help shift the government's mindset, while also getting out of my lab and seeing all the super cool stuff everyone else is doing!",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:$,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:sG,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"I was able to see DIU in action by taking “field trips” with the team to watch the space portfolio’s technology from simulations to rocket launches. Of course these opportunities have slowed during the COVID-19 pandemic, but that gave me the chance to get deep into my biggest project yet, the Hybrid Space Architecture, which I believe has the potential to transform our space connectivity.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:$,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:aP,marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:Cw,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"While I have many personal (but widely shared) frustrations with issues such as the recruitment and retention, stovepipes, and the pace of traditional DoD acquisitions, I believe the biggest issue DoD faces right now is climate change. More chaotic weather will pose an increasing national security risk, due to reduced food security, increased migration, more energetic natural disasters, and heightened tensions between nations. Interestingly, this problem is easily solvable through a combination of existing technology and policy, making it a perfect case for DIU.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:$,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:oL,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"I'm a space nerd, so the rapidly falling costs of launch and on-orbit assembly, tied to the expansion of ubiquitous broadband communications in space, are finally leading the human race to become the space-faring species we imagined in the 1960s. Meanwhile, the advent of more efficient and cleaner batteries, biofuels, and hydrogen storage, generated by renewable energy sources, will provide abundant energy for sustained growth while allowing new carbon sequestration technologies to restore our own planet to its pristine legacy.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:$,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:aP,marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:sH,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"I am currently re-reading an old favorite, \"Failure is Not an Option,\" by Gene Kranz, the legendary flight controller of the Apollo program. Every other chapter I jump to \"Screw It, Let's do it!\" and \"Losing my Virginity,\" autobiographies by Sir Richard Branson, the founder of one of our portfolio companies Virgin Galactic.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:$,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:aP,marks:[],data:{}},{nodeType:a,value:Cy,marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"The Hybrid Space Architecture project intends to link every satellite with high-speed internet, reducing satellite imagery latency from days to minutes. Applications range from troops identifying nearby threats to rapid response of firefighters in the California wildfires to catching dark ships illegally dumping oil. The \"space internet\" will provide broadband data to austere forward operating bases, isolated ground troops, and aircraft on long flights over open ocean (particularly useful for my rescue flights with the 130 Rescue Squadron). This connectivity further enables situational awareness between units engaged in combat and the mission operations center.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:$,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"If you could go back in time and work with DIU to solve a problem you experienced in the military, what would it be?",marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"A cyber officer recently said to me that we don't have planes, ships, and tanks anymore: we have computers that fly, computers that sail, and computers that drive. Industry has long since established standards for hardware modularity and software usability. Our flying, sailing and driving computers ought to be updated as easily as a Tesla downloading its software patch over the cellphone network every night, instead of the rare, expensive and laborious software update process I have experienced on HC-130J Combat Kings..",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:$,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"You have one foot in the private sector and one in DoD; what surprises you about the skills that do or do not translate between these worlds? What commercial best practice would you like to see the DoD adopt?",marks:[{type:l}],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:"My biggest surprise moving from the private sector into DoD was discovering how resigned everyone is to antiquated technology, bloated bureaucracy, and burdensome regulations. Military bureaucracy has installed far too many layers between the acquisition of technology and the end-users that any attempt to improve  the process feels futile. While regulations are designed to ensure the responsible use of taxpayer money on large programs of record, they also have the tendency to make folks the government more risk-averse. As any commercial entity would tell you, the risk of doing nothing is usually far worse than the risk of doing the wrong thing. Technology acquisitions need to adopt a more commercial process for assessing risk; bureaucracy needs to be pared down as if the CEO had to justify every hierarchical layer to the shareholders (taxpayers) instead of the board (Congress); and every regulation needs to carry a rationale, to justify when it may be disregarded and when it needs to be eliminated.",marks:[],data:{}}]},{nodeType:c,data:{},content:[{nodeType:a,value:i,marks:[],data:{}}]}]}}}]}},{metadata:{tags:[],concepts:[]},sys:{space:{sys:{type:b,linkType:d,id:e}},id:"1dvTGXIgv0NmKA0CT9NoQ5",type:j,createdAt:aka,updatedAt:aka,environment:{sys:{id:f,type:b,linkType:g}},publishedVersion:aD,revision:p,contentType:{sys:{type:b,linkType:k,id:S}},locale:h},fields:{title:CA,slug:"worldcongress2023",metaTitle:CB,metaSocialShareImage:{metadata:{tags:[],concepts:[]},sys:{space:{sys:{type:b,linkType:d,id:e}},id:akb,type:m,createdAt:sJ,updatedAt:sJ,environment:{sys:{id:f,type:b,linkType:g}},publishedVersion:v,revision:p,locale:h},fields:{title:CB,description:i,file:{url:akc,details:{size:sK,image:{width:r,height:x}},fileName:sL,contentType:t}}},header:{metadata:{tags:[],concepts:[]},sys:{space:{sys:{type:b,linkType:d,id:e}},id:"7s3ZY2mDn7dgMkMun0r9bZ",type:j,createdAt:"2023-07-18T18:40:14.727Z",updatedAt:"2023-07-18T19:38:52.758Z",environment:{sys:{id:f,type:b,linkType:g}},publishedVersion:y,revision:s,contentType:{sys:{type:b,linkType:k,id:C}},locale:h},fields:{adminTitle:"Header - Park is an Active Duty U.S. Air Force Major and a Project Manager supporting the Space Portfolio at the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU) in Mountain View, California. Prior to joining DIU, Maj. Park served as the Aide-de-Camp to Lieutenant General John Thompson, Commander of Space and Missile Systems Center at Los Angeles Air Force Base, California.",nodeType:a}],nodeType:c},{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[],value:Q,nodeType:a},{data:{},marks:[{type:l}],value:"Why did you want to work at DIU?",nodeType:a}],nodeType:c},{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[],value:"I wanted to come to DIU because I was excited about DIU’s mission to accelerate the adoption of commercial technology across the DoD. After experiencing working in a program office for a major defense acquisition program, and the bureaucracy that comes with it, the idea of executing smaller prototype projects with non-traditional defense contractors was refreshing and intriguing.",nodeType:a}],nodeType:c},{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[{type:l}],value:akn,nodeType:a}],nodeType:c},{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[],value:"I am currently the project manager for our Responsive Launch projects, where we are prototyping commercial solutions for low-cost, responsive access to space, to precisely place spacecraft into their mission-designed Low-Earth orbit. We are partnered with the Rocket System Launch Program and the DoD Space Test Program, and we have agreements with Rocket Lab, Virgin Orbit National Systems, Astra, SpinLaunch, Relativity Space, and ABL Space Systems.",nodeType:a}],nodeType:c},{data:{target:{metadata:{tags:[],concepts:[]},sys:{space:{sys:{type:b,linkType:d,id:e}},id:"79HKB65EzfP7esxWhZuudl",type:m,createdAt:aku,updatedAt:aku,environment:{sys:{id:f,type:b,linkType:g}},publishedVersion:y,revision:p,locale:h},fields:{title:"Virgin Orbit",description:"Maj. Park visiting Virgin Orbit facility with USD R&E Heidi Shyu, November 2022. (Courtesy photo)\n",file:{url:"\u002F\u002Fimages.ctfassets.net\u002F3nanhbfkr0pc\u002F79HKB65EzfP7esxWhZuudl\u002F658422978e10b70c5ffba686cce11b71\u002FVirgin_Orbit_Heidi_Shyu_1__1_.jpg",details:{size:305304,image:{width:sE,height:cM}},fileName:"Virgin Orbit Heidi Shyu 1 (1).jpg",contentType:w}}}},content:[],nodeType:G},{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[{type:l}],value:ako,nodeType:a}],nodeType:c},{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[],value:"I am truly inspired by the innovation in technology development and manufacturing advancements to push the state of the art. I’m also in awe of the resilience demonstrated by the companies we work with —they continue to make improvements to their products and systems, all while operating in a very volatile environment. ",nodeType:a}],nodeType:c},{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[{type:l}],value:"What are you currently reading?",nodeType:a}],nodeType:c},{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[],value:"I am currently reading “Becoming,” by Michelle Obama, and I love it because I find it very relatable and inspiring as a woman of color, mother, and professional. It’s difficult to navigate a male-dominated profession and balance motherhood, all while feeling guilty that I’m not able to give my 100 percent to everything, so this book makes me feel like I’m not alone - and reminds me that relationships are the most important above all.",nodeType:a}],nodeType:c},{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[{type:l}],value:"What are you currently celebrating \u002F what have been some recent wins for your team?",nodeType:a}],nodeType:c},{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[],value:"Relativity Space recently conducted their first launch of their Terran 1 rocket and met their goal of getting through Max-Q and also achieved stage separation, so that’s a huge accomplishment for the entire Relativity team! ",nodeType:a}],nodeType:c},{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[],value:"I’m also excited about Astra’s upcoming Spacetech Day, where they will showcase their progress on Launch System 2, and their new Astra Spacecraft Engine production facility. ",nodeType:a}],nodeType:c},{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[],value:"Rocket Lab has had two successful missions from their LC-2 at Wallops Island, enabled by the autonomous flight termination system, which is a major milestone in itself. ",nodeType:a}],nodeType:c},{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[],value:"ABL Space Systems  was recently awarded a Strategic Funding Increase  Program (STRATFI) for tactically responsive space demonstrations using their RS1 launch vehicle and mobile infrastructure. ",nodeType:a}],nodeType:c},{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[],value:"SpinLaunch completed their suborbital test campaign with 10 of 10 successful launches using their 33-meter mass accelerator, and they debuted their new line of satellite bus products, which complements their low-cost, high-cadence mass accelerator launch technology. ",nodeType:a}],nodeType:c},{data:{},content:[{data:{},marks:[],value:"\nVirgin Orbit established their U.K. spaceport, conducting the first launch from European soil, and despite the unfortunate second stage failure, they pioneered the process and are ready to do it again. Their anomaly resolution board is finalizing their investigation and are ready to return to
